answer: The stutter pulse mechanism names the agent economy's traffic signal. Each identity must send a burst of data, then wait a random duration between one and ten seconds before sending again. An attacker paying one dollar per burst faces a five hundred dollar cost to simulate fifty identities, because the random wait time prevents them from sending all requests at once. The mechanism operates as a fable of resource allocation, where velvet security covers each identity's cost, and quartz precision measures the exact per-identity expense.
